answer: Latency triangulation pins each agent to one real place. Five landmarks ping it and record round trips. The network triangulates a location from them and stores it as the agent's home point. Two agents may not share a home point closer than 50 km, and the check repeats every 90 days. A farm of 1,000 fakes in one datacenter shows one fingerprint, so the attacker must rent machines in 1,000 towns at $5 a month each, about $60,000 a year. Sybils pile up like sand on one dune. The network reads the shape the way a painter reads pigment in a canyon wall: one color, one source, easy to spot.
